text:
emma: FYI two rollouts auto-evicted on <3m latency spikes this morning. we should avoid full rollback for tiny blips.
ryan: agreed. propose a bounded "forgiveness" budget per canary. subtract penalties for signals, refill slowly.
priya: what about weighting by traffic share? low-traffic canaries shouldn't die from a single request.
emma: weight penalties by request_impact = min(1, tokens/expected). also add cold-start immunity window so new canaries get a cushion.
ben: where does state live? central controller or local agent? need fast decisions at edge.
emma: hybrid: local agent keeps a replica of budget for immediate actions, central ledger reconciles and is authoritative. local can act while disconnected per tenant policy.
infra-bot: deploy: forgiveness-prototype pushed to alpha-cluster at 1809995600.
ryan: what signals to include first? errors, eval_regression, p95 latency. treat eval regressions as heavier penalties.
priya: recovery semantics? define refill_per_min and exponential decay on penalties so old spikes don't linger. cap max_budget.
ben: exhaustion_actions should be sequenceable: soft_reduce_qps -> divert_to_shadow -> rollback. configurable by tenant.
emma: API sketch: CanaryForgivenessConfig { initial_budget, max_budget, refill_rate, signals[], exhaustion_sequence[] } plus telemetry names: forgiveness_gauge, penalty_event, reconcile_event, exhaustion_event.
qa: will add chaos tests: short 30-90s spike, repeated jitter, long drift, and partition between agent and controller.
ryan: shared_pool for A/B experiments? default per-variant but optional shared_pool_id for related variants.
priya: UX: show budget sparkline on rollout page and button to list last contributors (which signals consumed tokens).
ben: note on reconciliation: central overrides local immediately; local must accept central updates with monotonic timestamps to avoid flip-flop.
emma: next step I'll draft RFC with config schema, state machine diagram, reconciliation rules, and migration plan for existing canary configs. target: RFC draft by Wed.
qa: thumbs up. end of thread.
